title: Kenyan Chicken Wet Fry
community: Popular across all Kenyan communities — a restaurant favourite
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Chicken Wet Fry — chicken pieces fried until golden then finished in a thick, concentrated tomato, onion, and bell pepper sauce with Kenyan spices. Bold, saucy, and deeply satisfying — the chicken version of Kenya's most popular restaurant preparation.
longDesc: Chicken wet fry applies the same two-stage technique as beef wet fry — high-heat searing followed by finishing in a concentrated sauce. Because chicken cooks faster than beef, this is a quicker dish while delivering all the same bold character. The sauce should be thick enough to coat every piece generously.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces — bone-in, cut into serving pieces
steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat oil in a large pan over high heat. Brown chicken pieces for 4—5 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
In the same pan, cook onions until golden — 6 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and bell pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, and cumin. Cook for 5—7 minutes until thick.
Return chicken. Add ¼ cup water. Cover and cook for 15—20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Uncover and reduce sauce for 3—4 minutes until it clings to the chicken.
Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Brown the chicken in a very hot pan — this crust is the soul of wet fry.
Reduce the sauce at the end until it just coats the chicken — not swimming in liquid.
Bell pepper adds authentic wet fry character — do not skip it.
commonMistakes: Low heat for browning — produces pale, steamed chicken.
Too watery sauce — reduce until thick and clinging.

faqs.a: Yes — boneless thighs work well. Reduce the covered cooking time to 10—12 minutes.

cookingScience: Two-stage cooking: high heat creates Maillard browning on the chicken surface; gentle covered simmering then finishes cooking the interior without drying it out.
sustainabilityTips: Wet fry is ideal for using every part of the chicken — wings, drumsticks, and thighs all work well.
reheating: Reheat quickly in a pan with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Lower in fat than beef or goat wet fry.
culturalNote: Chicken wet fry is one of the most ordered dishes in Kenyan restaurants — beloved for its bold sauce, caramelised chicken, and the way it pairs perfectly with ugali or chapati.
regionalVariations: Coconut chicken wet fry — coastal style.
